full_judgment:
The Rule issued calling upon the Opposite parties to show cause as to why the judgment and decree dated 25-9-1995 passed by the learned Subordinate Judge, 1st Court, Khulna in Title Appeal No. 293 of 1993 upholding the judgment and decree dated 31-5-1993 passed by the learned Senior Assistant Judge, Khulna Sadar, Khulna in Title Suit No. 53 of 1987 should not be set-aside and/or pass such other or further order or orders as to this Court may seem fit and proper.

2. The facts give rise to the issuance of Rule in a nutshell are as follows: The present-opposite parties as plaintiffs instituted the Original Title Suit being No. 53 of 1987 for a decree of perpetual injunction restraining the defendant, Khulna Development Authority (here in after KDA) from entering into the suit property forcefully and demolishing the "Shib Bari Kali Mondir" situated in the suit land contending inter alia that the suit property appertaining to mouja Baniakhamar under Police Station Sonadanga of District Khulna within KDA Mazid Saroni in Plot No. A-45 measuring an area of 6.000 square feets is being used as "Shib Bari Kali Mondir" managed by a committee, on behalf of the Hindu community to perform their religious functions. In the suit property "Sree Sree Kali Mata Bigraha" has been established in hundred years back by the people of Hindu community, who were performing puja and other religious functions from the very beginning. The further case of the plaintiffs is such that for the purpose of puja and other religious functions an executive committee was formed in which the plaintiff No. 2 is Secretary. The further case of the plaintiffs is such that, as a place of worship, the Hindu community is regularly performing their religious programmers peacefully in the suit premises for more than hundred years and at this stage, KDA wanted to acquire the suit property illegally and tried to demolish the "Mondir" situated within the suit premises. In the suit premises besides the deity Kali, the other deities like "Durga" and others are standing and there is a boundary wall of the premises, but the defendant out of ill motive, giving threatening to the devotees, trying to dismantle the "Mondir" forcefully in the name of acquisition of the property for their so-called development work and as a result, finding no other alternative; the plaintiffs instituted the original suit for permanent injunction.

3. On the other hand, the case of the contesting defendant No. 01, KDA in short is thus, that the suit property has been acquired by KDA and the KDA gave compensation to the original owners of the property. The further case of the defendant-petitioner is such that, after acquisition of the property they have taken vacant possession of the land-in-dispute, which is a commercial Plot being No. A-45 measuring 6 (six)-kathas of land and has been leased out in favour of one Sheikh Ashraf Ali. The other Plot No. A-46 measuring the same quantum of land has been leased out in favour of one Kamruzzaman and the lease-holders are possessing the property.

4. The learned trial court during trial of the original suit after taking evidence from the sides of the respective parties decreed the suit on contest by the judgment and decree dated 31-5-1993 and 7-6-1993 respectively.

5. Being aggrieved the defendant preferred a Title Appeal being No. 293 of 1993 in the court of learned District Judge, Khulna which was transmitted to the 1st Court of the learned the then Subordinate judge, Khulna for hearing and disposal and the learned Appellate Court hearing the appeal disallowed the same affirming the judgment and decree passed by the trial court by the impugned judgment and decree dated 25-9-1995 and 1-10-1995 respectively.

6. Being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the impugned judgment and decree the defendant has preferred this revisional application in this court under section 115(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure and obtained the Rule.

7. During hearing of the Rule Mr Md Motahar Hossain Sazu, the learned Advocate appeared on behalf of the petitioner while Mr Abul Kalam Mainuddin, the learned Advocate appeared on behalf of the opposite parties.

8. The learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioner submits that, the learned trial court as well as the learned Appellate Court committed illegality and irregularity during disposal of the original suit and its subsequent appeal. The learned Advocate further submits that the plaintiff No. 2 applied for allotment of the suit land to them as it was acquired by KDA and thereby the plaintiffs are stopped from filing the suit against the defendant. The learned Advocate also submits that the suit is barred by Emergency Requisition of Property Act, 1948 but the learned trial court as well as the learned Appellate Court failed to appreciate the law and without realizing the facts and circumstances of the case erroneously decided the merit of the suit and its subsequent appeal in favour of the plaintiffs and, as such, the Rule is liable to be made absolute.

9. As against the aforesaid submission of the learned Advocate for the petitioner, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the opposite parties opposing the Rule submits that, neither the trial court nor the appellate court committed any illegality or infirmity in deciding the merit of the suit and its subsequent appeal. The learned Advocate further submits that the plaintiffs have acquired valid, right, title, interest and possession in the suit property by way of adverse possession for more than hundred years, which is being used as "Puja Mondir". The learned Advocate also submits that inasmuch as the suit premises is a place of worship of the Hindu community at the locality, there was no scope for requisition of that property by KDA and the land-in-dispute can not be vested to the Government by any proceedings. The learned Advocate submits that the people of the locality from the ancient time are performing their religious functions in the suit premises, which is commonly known as "Shib Bari Kali Mondir" and in the suit premises there is a Kali deity and other deities & these are being used for various religious activities of the Hindu community. The learned Advocate argued that the property is out and out such a property which is being used for religious functions including "puja" and other related affairs of the Hindu community. The learned Advocate lastly submits that the learned trial court at the time of disposal of the original suit rightly after proper assessment of evidence in its true perspective arrived at a conclusive decision as to the nature and character of the suit property and accordingly, decided the merit of the suit in favour of the plaintiffs and subsequently, the Appellate Court also at the time of disposal of the appeal on proper appreciation of law, evidence and factual aspects of the case decided the merit of the appeal in favour of the respondent therein, and there is no misreading or non-reading of evidence or non consideration of material facts resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice, by which the impugned judgment and decree can be interfered with.

10. In order to appreciate the submission of the learned Advocates, on perusal of the impugned judgment and decree dated 25-9-1995 passed in Title Appeal No. 293 of 1993 along with the judgment and decree passed by the learned trial court dated 31-5-1993 in Title Suit No. 53 of 1987 including all other relevant papers and the evidences adduced from the sides of the respective parties, it transpires that the plaintiffs to the original suit in order to obtain a decree of perpitual injunction restraining the defendant, KDA from entering into the schedule property forcefully and dismantling the standing "Kali Mondir" of the suit property filed the original suit and going through the plaint, I find that it is the specific contention/case of the plaintiffs that "Shib Bari Kali Mondir" represented by the secretary, Shib Bari Sarbojanin Puja Committee, Khulna that the suit property is being possessed by the Hindu community of the locality as 'Shib Bari Kali Mondir' for years together, which is more than hundred years. It was further contended by the plaintiff-opposite parties in their pleadings that in the suit property, there is a deity "Sree Sree Kali Ma ta Bigraha" and "Durga" with other bigrahas and the Hindu community of the locality use to perform their religious activities regularly in that "Mondir" and in the year 1947 during partition the persons engaged in looking after and managing the "Mondir" left this country and in respect of the ownership of the property, due to the ignorance of the local Hindu community, no paper was obtained or record of right was prepared, but the facts remains that the local Hindu community without any disturbance or objection from any corner, use to possess the suit premises as before, for more than hundred years openly and adversely within the knowledge of all, including the defendant, petitioner, KDA. It is the positive case of the plaintiffs that the defendant-petitioner have no authority in the suit premises, but only to grab the property in the name of requisition through Additional Deputy Commissioner, Khulna sent an office memo being No. 3421 dated 10-6-1982 illegally for making a decision after consultation with the local Hindu community, but without taking decision there under, all on a sudden, on 5th Falgun of 1393 BS the defendant through their officials tried to destroy the "Shib Bari Kali Mondir" touching the religious sentiment of the Hindu community, causing serious difficulties to that community, which constrained the plaintiffs to institute the original suit for permanent injunction. It was asserted by the plaintiffs that, there is an apprehension of imminent criminal breach of peace in the locality with regard to the suit premises due to the activities of the defendant KDA.

11. The learned trial court during trial of the original suit after taking evidence from the sides of the respective parties decreed the suit on contest which was subsequently affirmed by the appellate court.

12. On meticulous assessment of the connected papers and evidence on records, I find that the defendant KDA, Khulna in their pleadings alleged that for their urgent need the suit property is required and accordingly the property was acquisitioned and according to their averments mentioned in the written statement, this property comprises of 6.00 Kathas in Plot No. A-45 and 6.00 khatas in Plot No. A-46, has been leased out for commercial purpose in favour of one Sheikh Ashraf Ali and Kamruzzaman and there has been allotment to that effect in favour of the allotees, but the fact remains that, no where within the pleadings of the defendant, KDA it is adverted that in what case; the property-in-dispute has been requisitioned and under what process it was allegedly requisitioned for the purpose of construction of a road for development work as alleged from their side.

13. Consulting the evidence led from the sides of the respective parties it further transpires that, the defendant-petitioner during trial of the original suit submitted an official gazette marked as Exhibit-"Ka" which is not specified for specification of the suit premises and its area. Besides this, the gazette notification is with regard to an Enrollment Case No. 12086 with reference to a Waqf Estate, which is a third case. From the documentary evidences filed by the defendant, I also find that the paper which is furnished from the side of the defendant-petitioner vide Exhibit-"Gha" is a proposed plan, showing a map including the cost of a project, and it is not identical with the suit property.

14. Vis-a-vis, the plaintiffs in order to establish their case have adduced 3 (three) witnesses. PW 1 is the plaintiff No. 2 Amritalal Saha. This witness in his testimony corroborated their plaint case and categorically testified that in the suit premises "Shib Bari Kali Mondir" is situated, which is being used by the Hindu community of the locality for the last hundred years and in that `Mondir; 'puja' and other religious functions are performed regularly, and beside that "Kali Bigraha" there exist "Durga", "Manosa" and other Bigrahs and these are also regularly used for the religious activities of the Hindu community. PW 1 at a stage of his testimony testified that, they are not law knowing persons and could not enter into any proceedings of requisition by KDA With regard to the cause of action of this suit the plaintiff No. 2 categorically testified that on 5th Falgun, 1393 BS the KDA authority threatened them to dismantle the 'Mondir'. During cross-examination this witness who is the Secretary of the 'Mondir' testified at a stage that he is the Secretary of the Mondir Committee and there is an organogram of the 'Mondir', according to which the regular works of the 'Mondir' are going on. The plaintiff No. 2 also testified in a reply to a question during his cross-examination that he knew that the lands of 'Mondir' can not be requisitioned, even then; knowing about the alleged requision of the property by KDA after receiving a letter, they were willing to take allotment of the suit property for the purpose of their religious functions and for want of that, for taking allotment they met with the concerned authority, Additional Deputy Commissioner, but failed.

15. PW 2 is one Sonju Kumar Roy Chowdhury. This witness testified in support of the possession of the plaintiff and existence of "Shib Bari Kali Mondir" in the suit property. PW 2 in his deposition categorically testified that he knows the suit property, in where there is a "Mondir" for years together and he has heard that the 'Mondir' is functioning since hundred years and he is finding the pucca wall with ceiling made of CI sheets, in the suit premises and permanent 'Bigrahas' within these rooms, in where `puja' is continuing regularly throughout the year by the Hindu community. During cross-examination this witness testifies that, previously the shed was made of "gol pata" and after that CI sheets are used for the sheds of the huts. In a reply to a question from the side of the defendants, PW 2 testified at a stage that he is a member of the Mondir Committee for the last 5/6 years.

16. PW 3 Bimol Krishna Sarker is another possession witness of the plaintiffs. This witness in his testimony testified that he knows the suit premises, in where there is a "Kali Mondir" and it is hundred years old, and 'puja' is performed therein regularly. This witness categorically testified that in the suit property there exist bigrahas of 'Kali', 'Durga' and 'Manosa'. PW 3 like the former witness in a voice testified that, if this 'Mondir' is dismantled, definitely; it will create adverse sensation in the sentiment of the Hindu community. In the cross-examination PW 3 testified at a stage that he resides in the neibouring area of this "Shib Bari Mondir" since 1965 AD.

17. On the other hand, the witness No. 01 of the defendant-petitioner is an Office Assistant of KDA Abdul Aziz by name. This witness in his testimony testified that KDA has requisitioned the suit property and it is under possession of KDA Subsequently, the same witness of the defendant, testified that the plaintiffs have pucca huts in the suit premises which is a "puja mandop" and it was constructed by the plaintiff. The witness No. 01 of the defendant in his cross examination testified at a stage that in the suit property, there is a "Mondir" and in the year 1987, in the month of February; the construction work of the 'Mondir' was started and he (DW 1) does not know as to why KDA could not take any step against the construction work of the plaintiffs. In a reply to another question from the side of the plaintiffs, DW 1 testified that they gave a lease deed in favour of Ashraf All on 15-3-1988 and at that time also, the 'Mondir' was there (suit premises) with pacca-wall. DW 1 frankly conceded in his deposition that he does not know; as to whether Ashraf Ali obtained possession in the suit premises. In another stage of the testimony, DW 1 frankly testified in the following way: কোন মন্দির সম্পত্তি কে.ডি.এ.হুকুম দখল করে না। কে.ডি.এ. সার্ভে করিয়া জমি হুকুম দখল করে। নালিশী জমি কে সার্ভে করিয়াছিল জানি না।

18. DW 2 Kali Pado Das is a Law Assistant of KDA. This witness in his testimony testified that, part of Plot No. 1515 has been requisitioned and it has been marked as Plot No. A-45. DW 2 in his deposition before the trial court in the last portion admits that they did not file any paper showing that the suit 'Mondir' is in Plot No. A-45. This witness also testified that he does not know, what is the area of suit Mondir.

19. Analyzing the evidence on records critically, I find that the learned trial court as well as the appellate court rightly held concurrently in their judgment and decree that the plaintiffs to the suit have successfully proved that the suit property is used as 'Mondir' for the Hindu community of the concern locality and regularly puja and other religious activities are going on there, for more than hundred years. From the admission of the defendant's witnesses, the case of the plaintiff has also been corroborated and I have come-across from careful scrutiny over the evidence on records that the defendant KDA has measurably failed to discharge their onus of proof that the suit property has really been acquisitioned or requisitioned, pursuant to any lawful proceedings. There is no paper form their side, showing the alleged acquisition or requisition of the suit property. Furthermore, it has been well proved by sufficient credible tangible evidence from the side of the plaintiff-opposite parties that the suit property is being possessed by the plaintiffs for more than hundred years, openly and adversely within the knowledge of everybody, including the defendant KDA, which is practically admitted from the side of the defendant's witnesses in their testimonies.

<u>20. Apart form this, it is the mandate of the Constitution of the People’s Republic of Bangladesh vides Article 41, that the freedom of religion is one of the fundamental right of each and every citizen, and our sacred Constitution, which is the supreme law of the country, has guaranteed that. In this regard, Sub-Article (1) of Article 41 of the Constitution of Bangladesh provides,</u>

<u>"Subject to law, public order and morality.</u>

<u>(a)	every citizen has the right to profess, practise or propagate any religion;</u>

<u>(b)	every religious community or denomination has the right to establish, maintain and manage its religious institutions."</u>

<u>21. This right to religion and religious institutions been reflected in several decisions of our Apex Court given the cases of Matilal Sikder vs Binodini Dasi reported in 28 DLR (AD) 5, Sree Sree Dasha Bhuja Mata vs jamila Khatun Bibi reported in 9 BLT (AD) 211 and in the case of Falguni Majumder vs Mokbul Hossain Biswas reported in 4 BLC (AD) 5 and this court in the case of Azahar Ali Miah vs Dimla Raj Debottar Estate reported in 5 ALR 166. Hence, apparently; it is a decided matter that the property which is being used as 'Mondir' by the Hindu community for years together can not be requisitioned or acquisitioned what so ever forthwith touching the religious sentiment of the people of the Republic.</u>

<u>22. Besides this, section 3 of the Emergency Requisition of Property Act, 1948 (XII of 1948) does not empower the Government to requisition the property of a subject for the benefit of a particular individual. Under section 14(2) of the Requisition of Property Act, 1948 the Government is empowered to make alteration of any act done by them, if any requisition is made violating the requisition Rules. In this context. I find support in the case law reported in 12 DLR (SC) 161.</u>

23. Having gone through the admission of KDA as it transpires from their pleading's case, cited in the written statement it has become crystal clear that, not for development work but for commercial purpose the suit property has been allegedly acquisitioned by the defendant-petitioner KDA.

24. In the foregoing narrative, having regard to the facts, circumstances and the discussions referred to above, I am constrained to hold such a view that the Rule has got no merit to succeed, inasmuch as; there is no illegality or infirmity or no such misreading or non-reading of evidence or non-consideration of material facts resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice, by dint of which, the impugned judgment and decree can be interfered with.

25. In the result; the Rule is discharged.

The impugned judgment and decree dated 25-9-1995 passed by the learned Subordinate Judge, 1st Court, Khulna in Title Appeal No. 293 of 1993 upholding the judgment and decree dated 31-5-1993 passed by the learned Senior Assistant Judge, Khulna Sadar, Khulna in Title Suit No. 53 of 1987is hereby affirmed.

26. However, there will be no order as to costs.

27. Communicate the judgment and order at once.

Send down the lower Court's records immediately.

End.

full_judgment:
Md Nuruzzaman J: On an application under section 115(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure calling upon the opposite party to show cause as to why the impugned judgment and order complained of in the petition moved in Court today should not be set aside and/or pass such other of further order or orders as to this Court seem fit and proper.

2. The material facts, relevant for, disposal of the instant Rule, in short, are that, on 19-5-2016 the opposite party No. 3 filed an application under Order IX, rule 9A read with section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure (hereinafter to be referred as the Code) in the Court of Joint District Judge, 3rd Court, Dhaka for setting aside the order of dismissal for default passed on 11-5-2016 in Miscellaneous Case No. 27 of 2014 and restored the said to its original file and number.

3. It has been narrated in the revisional application that the instant petitioner as plaintiff instituted Title Suit being No. 476 of 1981 before the Joint District Judge, 3rd Court, Dhaka against the opposite party Nos. 1 and 2 for settlement of account in respect of the amounts of sale and installation commission carried by the plaintiff.

4. The defendant Nos. 1 and 2 contested the suit by filing written statement. The suit was dismissed on 22-12-1986 on contest.

5. Plaintiff preferred the First Appeal No. 81 of 1987 before the High Court Division of the Supreme Court of Bangladesh.

6. During the pendency of the said appeal the defendant No. 1 NCR Corporation appointed the Leads Corporation Ltd. as their exclusive distributor for Bangladesh with effect from 1-8-1992. On 1-8-1992 an advertisement was published in the Bangladesh Observer in this regard. Knowing this fact the plaintiff appellant filed an application before the Hon'ble High Court Division for adding the Leads Corporation Ltd. as respondent No. 3 in the pending First Appeal No. 81 of 1987. The Hon'ble Court was pleased to issue the Rule calling upon the opposite party as to why the Leads Corporation Ltd. should not be added as party. The Leads Corporation Ltd. appeared before the Court through its engaged lawyer.

7. On hearing both the sides the application was allowed and Rule was made absolute on 26-8-2003. Thereafter, on hearing both the sides first/Appeal was allowed on 25-5-2009 in the preliminary form by setting aside the judgment and decree dated 22-8-1986 passed in title suit No. 476 of 1981. Thereafter, the Hon'ble High Court Division was also pleased to pass an order directing the trial Court to appoint an expert/commissioner to examine the connected books of account and other papers of the defendants and to ascertain the amount of commission due to the plaintiff from the defendants from 1976 up to 1981.

8. The trial Court appointed Chartered Accountant directing him to submit an audit report and statement of account for ascertaining the amount of commission due to the plaintiff without any objection from parties to the suit. The trial Court got the audit report and statement of account. Thereafter, the trial Court passed the final decree on 8-8-2010 treating the said statement of account and audit report as part of the final decree without any objection from any party.

9. The plaintiff appellant as petitioner by dint of judgment and decree dated 8-8-2010 filed an Execution Case being Execution Case No. 07 of 2013.

10. The Leads Corporation Ltd. opposite party No. 3 after about 4 years on 29-6-2014 filed an Miscellaneous Case under Order IX, rule 13 read with 151 of the Code being Miscellaneous Case No. 27 of 2014 before the learned Joint District Judge, 3rd Court, Dhaka for setting aside the final decree dated 12-8-2010 without explaining the delay of 216 days in filing of the said Miscellaneous Case.

11. The plaintiff as opposite party contested the miscellaneous case upon filing written objection.

12. The Miscellaneous Case No. 27 of 2014 was fixed for hearing on 11-5-2016. The defendant petitioner on that date filed an application for adjournment without assigning any reason.

13. The trial Court was pleased to reject the application as none of the Advocate appeared in Court and moved the application and further directed the parties to get ready at once and appear in the Court for hearing of the Miscellaneous Case. However, on that date till 4-30 pm none of the learned Advocate was appeared on behalf of the defendant petitioner and, as such the learned Joint District Judge dismissed the said Miscellaneous Case.

14. on 19-5-2016 petitioner as applicant instead of preferring an appeal as per provision

of law against the order of dismissal of the Miscellaneous Case filed an application under Order IX, rule 9A read with section 151 of the Code without giving any notice upon the opposite party for restoring the Miscellaneous Case by setting aside the order of dismissal dated 11-5-2016.

15. The petitioner on 19-5-2016 without giving notice to the plaintiff or the learned Advocate of the plaintiff opposite party most illegally, arbitrarily and without applying judicial mind upon ex party hearing of the learned Advocate for the applicant allowed the said application.

16. Hence, being aggrieved by the impugned order dated 19-5-2016 the decree holder as petitioner preferred the instant revisional application and obtained the instant Rule with an order of stay.

17. Mr ASM Rahmatullah with Mr Khaled Saifullah, the learned Advocates appearing for the petitioner has submitted that on 19-5-2016 the opposite party as applicant without giving any notice or serving any copy of the application to the plaintiff opposite party or his Advocate filed an application under Order IX, rule 9A read with section 151 of the Code for restoring the Miscellaneous Case which was allowed ex parte by the learned Joint District Judge, 3rd Court, Dhaka without applying his judicial mind because a Miscellaneous Case filed under Order IX, rule 13 of the Code if dismissed for default is not revisable, rather, it is appealable under sub Rule (d) of Rule 1 of Order XLIII of the Code but in the instant case Miscellaneous Case petitioner without invoking the proper provision of law filed the vexatious application and the learned judge of the Court below without considering the legal proposition as laid down for redress for the aggrieved party in Order XLIII invoked the jurisdiction under Order IX, rule 9A read with section 151 of the Code and, as such, committed serious error of law.

18. He further added that the learned Joint District Judge failed to consider the facts and circumstances that the petitioner herein as an applicant filed the petition for restoration of the Miscellaneous Case without serving any copy of the petition to the learned Advocate for the opposite party or the opposite party invoking wrong provision of law and the learned Joint District Judge allowed the application upon misconception taking view that the applicant filed the petition within time and has explained the reason satisfactorily, therefore, allowed the application with cost of Taka 1,000 according to provision of Rule 9A of Order IX, of the Code which cannot be sustained in law as Rule 9A of the Order IX of the Code can be applicable only for the plaintiff who filed the suit which was dismissed according to provision of Rule 8 of the Code not for the Miscellaneous Case and, as such, the learned Joint District Judge committed an error of law resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of the justice which is liable to be set aside.

19. Mr Khaled Saifullah the learned Advocate in support of his submission relied upon the decisions reported 45 DLR (AD) 37, PLD 1953 Dhaka, 183, 32 DLR 57.

20. On contra, Mr Tanjib-ul Alam, the learned Advocate appearing for the opposite party No. 3. Who contested the Rule by filing counter affidavit stating, inter alia, that the opposite party precisely and specifically mentioned in the time petition the reasons for adjournment? The Bench Officer of the Court assured that the time petition of the opposite party No. 3 would be accepted, since, there is no objection from the opposite party and accordingly nothing was written on the said petition which might indicate that the opposite party has no any objection whatsoever. Upon such assurance from the Bench Officer of the Court the learned Counsel left the Court believing that the time petition would be allowed. It has been further narrated that the conducts of the Court's Bench Officer attributed to the disposal of the Miscellaneous Case No. 27 of 2014 as elaborated in the application dated 19-5-2016 which caused injustice to the opposite party No. 3 and since the circumstance causing the dismissal of the Miscellaneous Case No. 27 of 2014 stand on a different footing the trial Court was right invoking its inherent power under section 151 of the Code for setting aside the dismissal order dated 11-5-2016.

21. Mr Tanjib-ul-Alam with Ms. Nazmun-Binte-Islam, the learned Advocates appearing on behalf of the opposite party has further submitted that it is well settled that the jurisdiction under section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure is a discretionary one which is to be exercised where it is called for securing the ends of justice. Since, the facts and circumstance of dismissal of the Miscellaneous Case No. 27 of 2014 were exceptional the Hon'ble Court has rightly invoked its inherent power restoring the Miscellaneous Case and, as such, committed no error of law.

22. Mr Alam, has further added that the petitioner with ill motives challenged the order dated 19-5-2016 after passing of 325 days from the date of the said order by relying on facts and laws which have no legal basis in the instant application and, as such, the Court below committed no error of law which does not call for any interference by this Court. Ms. Nazmun-Binte-Islam, the learned Advocate relied to the case of Hosne Ara Begum vs Chairman, Court of Settlement, 46 DLR (AD) 9, Chand Biswas vs Khaleque, 51 DLR (AD) 551, 29 DLR (SC) 185, 26 DLR 124, 38 DLR 258.

23. We have anxiously considered the submissions advanced by the learned Advocates of the respective parties. We have perused the impugned order dated 19-5-2016 and order dated 11-5-2016. We have carefully examined the precedents referred by the Advocates of the respective parties. We have also perused the application dated 19-5-2016 under Order IX, rule 9A read with section 151 of the Code. On perusal the application for restoration of the Miscellaneous Case being No. 27 of 2014 it manifests that the learned Advocate specifically narrated the following facts that on 11-5-2016 by his associate lawyer filed an application for adjournment due to sickness he could not appeared in Court. However, up to 11-30 am Case file was not found in Bench, the Bench Officer and staffs informed the lawyer that প্রতিপক্ষের আপত্তি না থাকিলে সময়ের আবেদন শুনানীর জন্য প্রয়োজন নাই। সময় হইয়া যাইবে। Thereafter, the learned lawyer inquired about the file of the case and wanted to see the same in that time it was also informed that the application has been sent to the sheresta to find out the record. The learned lawyer of the petitioner went to the sheresta and inquired about the file from where it was also told that সময়ের আবেদন থাকিলে মঞ্জুর হইয়া যাইবে in such facts and circumstances the learned Advocate awaiting to have next date of the instant case. However, on 18-5-2016 the learned Advocate for the petitioner found in the cause list that the Miscellaneous Case No. 27 of 2014 was dismissed.

24. So, in the given facts of the instant case the moot question before us whether an application under Rule 9A of the Order IX read with section 151 or an appeal under Rule (d) (1) of the Order LXIII would be invoked for restoration of the Miscellaneous Case dismissed for default filed under Rule 13 of the Order IX of the Code?

25. We are of the view that to settle the matter and for better understanding and ready reference the provision of Rules 8 and 9A of the Order IX of the Code may be reproduced herein below:

26. R. 8 Procedure where defendant only appears. Where the defendant appears and the plaintiff does not appear when the suit is called on for hearing, the Court shall make an order that the suit be dismissed, unless the defendant admits the claim, or part thereof, in which case the Court shall pass a decree against the defendant upon such admission, and, where part only of the claim has been admitted, shall dismiss the suit so far as it relates to the remainder.

27. R.9A. Directly setting aside dismissal. —(1) Notwithstanding anything contained in rule 9 or any other law, the Court may, in order to avoid delay and expedite disposal, directly set aside the dismissal without requiring the plaintiff to adduce evidence to satisfy it about sufficient causes as required under rule 9, but requiring him to pay such cost not exceeding one thousand taka as it may deem appropriate and determine:

Provided that the dismissal under rule 8 shall not be set aside under this rule, unless an application, supported by affidavit, praying for setting aside the order of dismissal is made to the Court within thirty days of the date on which the order of dismissal is made:

Provided further that no dismissal shall be set aside more than once under this rule.

(2) As soon as an order under sub-rule (1) is made setting aside ex parte dismissal, the Court shall cause notice thereof to be served at the cost of the plaintiff upon the defendant who appeared in the suit.

28. Comments. Since this newly inserted rule does not in any way curtail the provision of rule 9, it merely allows a well to do plaintiff to be negligent in conducting his case rand gives him one more chance. In that view of the matter, the amendment may not serve the purpose of reducing in delay in adjudication.

29. On perusal the provision of Rule 9A of Order IX of the Code it is clearly divulged that this provision of law would be applicable only for the plaintiff when a suit is dismissed for default, however, the provision of the said Rule cannot be applicable for restoration of a Miscellaneous Case dismissed for default which was filed under Rule 13 of Order IX of the Code at the instance of the defendant.

30. We are of the considered view that invoking the provision of Rule 9A of Order IX and section 151 of the Code would not be the legal and lawful recourse of remedy for seeking redress for restoration of Miscellaneous Case because of the provision of sub Rule (d) of Rule I of Order XLIII of the Code wherein there is a specific provision of law for restoration the Miscellaneous case dismissed for default filed under the provision of Rule 13 of the Order IX of the Code.

31. In support of our view we can place reliance to the case of Abdul Kader Chowdhury vs Nurul Islam reported 43 DLR (AD) 128.

32. However, in the present Case the learned Advocate for the opposite party argued that it is the mistake of the Court as it was the mistake of the Bench Officer of the Court below.

33. To ascertain the truth we have perused the order. On perusal of the impugned order and the application for restoration of the Miscellaneous Case we do not find any substance in the submission of the learned Advocate for the opposite party that it was a mistake of the Court and the Court admitted the mistake and restored Miscellaneous Case only for the mistake of the Bench Officer or of the Court itself.

<u>34. Rather, on a bare reading of the language of the impugned order it appears that the learned Joint District Judge was of the opinion that the application filed under Rule 9A of Order IX of the Code read with section 151 was within time, so, as per provision of Rule 9A of the Order IX of the Code imposing the cost and on deposition the same the application of restoration was allowed.</u>

35. It would be noteworthy to reproduce the section 151 of the Code for ready reference is runs as follows:

S. 151. Saving of inherent powers of Court.—Nothing in this Code shall be deemed to limit or otherwise affect the inherent power of the Court to make such orders as may be necessary for the ends of justice or to prevent abuse of the process of the Court.

<u>36. It is the age-old legislative recognition and well settled maxim that every Court has inherent power to act "ex debito justitiae i.e. to do the real and substantial justice in dispensation of or to prevent abuse of process of the Court invoking the inherent jurisdiction of the Court.</u>

37. In 1868, his lordship Mr Justice Peocock, Hon'ble CJ observed "Since the laws are general rules, they cannot regulate for all time to come so as to make express provisions against all the cases that may possibly happen  It is the duty of the judges to apply the Laws, not only to what appears to be regulated by their express dispositions but to all the cases to which a just application may be made, and which appear to be comprehended either within the express sence of the law or within the consequences that may be gathered from it."

38. Ref: Hurro vs Shoorodhonee, 9 WR 402; Monohar vs Harilal, AIR 1962 SC 527.

39. It has further observed and long line of catena of maxim of law as well settled by the apex Court of the Country as Well as the sub continent that

"Though the power is very wide and residuary in nature and not controlled by any other provision of the Code, it is not to be exercised if its exercise is inconsistent, or comes in conflict, with any provisions of the Code.

40. Ref: Mama Reo vs Vimala Kumare, AIR 1960 AP 216. The Hon'ble Appellate Division to the case of Bangladesh vs Luxmi Bibi held that

"As this power is residual in nature to do justice and to avoid abuse of process of the Court this power can not be exercise when there is an alternative remedy available to the party" reported 46 DLR (AD) 158."

41. On the facts and circumstances we find that the submissions advanced by the learned Advocate for the petitioner bears substance. We have gone through the precedent referred by both the sides. On perusal of the precedents referred by learned Advocate of the opposite party, we although are not disagreeing with the aforesaid principle of law enunciated by their lordships. However, we find that the facts and circumstance of the present case and the referred cases are quite distinguishable. On the other hand the precedent referred by the learned Advocate for the petitioner is quite applicable in the present case.

42. Therefore, we find support and good deal of force in the submission of the learned Advocate for the petitioner.

43. Thus, the Rule having merit, it succeeds.

44. In the result, the Rule is made absolute and the impugned judgment and order dated 19-5-2016 is hereby set aside.

The office is directed to communicate the judgment at once.

End.
